rationale: I re-derived all 12 of my round-1 asks. 11 are addressed, and 1 was correctly refuted (registerLandedPanel exists in fixtures.go; my grep was too narrow). The new grounding claims check out: the FindLandedMerge consumer table is complete, and reattest/firstParentMergesFn, the ExactSecondParentMerges location, the phase functions and all named tests are confirmed. One substantive new issue: OQ-9 claims #255's two defects are both fixed, but the spec's own Background A shows the reported bead (title-fallback lineage plus a dotted ID, outside the --parent set) becomes an unclaimable N3 near-miss. Defect 2 (the exclusion) is therefore kept by design, and the 'exactly the set readiness can evaluate' premise is false. Smaller items: the 'target-pinned' fallback claim does not hold for the MergeInto subject; R2.2's no-escape waist conflicts with phase.Cache's explicit -n 0 while core is declared not impacted; AC-11(iii) is ambiguous against R4.2's exclusion; and the installed-copy wording is wrong.
concrete_changes_required: OQ-9 / Goal (a): stop claiming both #255 defects are fixed. State that defect 1 (zero instead of naming) is fixed. Defect 2 (the exclusion) is fixed only for the N1 detached-plan-form class and the R2 cap class. The issue's actual shape (title-fallback lineage plus a dotted ID outside --parent) is an N3 near-miss that stays unclaimable via next by design, until 129b's phase-lineage unification. Correct Option N's 'exactly the set readiness and complete can already evaluate'; readiness evaluates a superset via the [NNN] title fallback and beadIndex's prefix-free '.N'.

Background D.2 / ADR Touchpoints (i): drop 'target-pinned' for the 'Merge bead/<id>' (MergeInto) form, which carries no target, or define a structural target check. Say whether merge_resumption.go's accepted 'Merge bead/<id> into <target>' form can land and whether R4.2 admits it.

R2.2: specify the waist's behaviour when an existing caller passes an explicit '-n','0' (phase.Cache x3, approve/plan.go queryExistingChildren). Either tolerate or strip it, or declare internal/phase (core) impacted.
AC-11(iii): state that X and Y each land with their own spec-branch merge, or explain what identifies X given R4.2 excludes 'Merge branch 'bead/X' into bead/Y'.

Impacted Domains: the installed .claude/skills/ms-bead-impl/SKILL.md has no override prose (0 matches). Describe it as a refresh, not a removal. Classify the flag-name comments at internal/bead/clarify.go:100 and bdcli.go:368, and fence historical_skills/ from edits.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: OQ-9 says both #255 defects are fixed, but by the spec's own Background A the reported bead stays unclaimable
findings.detail: gh issue 255 defect 2 is 'the exclusion itself': a bead that bd calls ready and ready-check passes (MF-1..MF-4 PASS) is dropped by the claim path. Background A identifies the shape: ready-check PASS through the '[NNN]' title fallback (phase.FindEpicForBeadWithCache) plus a dotted ID (readiness.beadIndex reads any trailing .N and does not check the <E> prefix), while the bead is absent from 'bd ready --parent E'. Such a bead cannot be an R1.1 member, and per Background A even a detached <E>.<N> stays in the --parent set. It is an N3 near-miss, recovery 'bd show <id> --json', 'mindspec next claims only plan beads'. So 129 fixes defect 1 (named instead of zero) but keeps defect 2 by design. OQ-9 redefines defect 2 as 'the three answers now disagree visibly', which is not what the issue reports. OQ-9 Option N's claim that the plan-bead set is 'exactly the set readiness and complete can already evaluate' is false for the same reason: readiness evaluates a strict superset (title-fallback lineage plus any '.N' suffix), which is #255's three-answers shape. State honestly that #255 defect 2 is closed only for the N1 class (and the R2 cap class), and that N3 exclusion is a deliberate decision, deferred to 129b's phase-lineage unification. Do not claim #255 is fully fixed, or say what closes it.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: the fallback is called 'source- and target-pinned', but mindspec's own landing subject names no target
findings.detail: Background D.2 says 'a source- and target-pinned fallback', and ADR Touchpoints (i) says 'with the spec branch as its target'. R4.2 admits exactly 'Merge bead/<id>', which is gitutil.MergeInto's form (gitops.go:325 fmt.Sprintf("Merge %s", sourceBranch)), and 'Merge branch 'bead/<id>' into <spec-branch>'. Only the second carries a target. mindspec's own landings, including the merge_resumption.go path, which also accepts 'Merge <src>' and 'Merge <src> into ', always use the first form. So the target pin is unenforceable for exactly the subjects that matter. A 'Merge bead/X' made into any other branch that later becomes reachable is admitted. Corroboration still needs an exact second parent, so this is not obviously a false PASS, but the text claims more than the code can check. Either drop 'target-pinned' for the MergeInto form, or define a structural target check. Note also that merge_resumption.go accepts 'Merge bead/X into <target>' as a mindspec-written form, while the R4.2 exact set omits it; say whether that form can land.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: R2.2's 'no cap escape' waist conflicts with existing internal/phase callers while core is declared not impacted
findings.detail: R2.2: ListJSON appends -n 0 unconditionally and 'a caller cannot pass -n/--limit through them'. phase.Cache already calls listJSONFn (= bead.ListJSON) with '-n','0' at cache.go:247, 287 and 303, and approve/plan.go queryExistingChildren does the same at plan.go:1187. If 'cannot pass' is enforced by refusal, internal/phase must change, but core is declared NOT impacted. If the waist strips or tolerates an explicit '-n 0', say so. Specify the waist's behaviour on an explicit '-n 0' from existing callers.

findings.title: AC-11(iii) seems to contradict R4.2's exclusion as written
findings.detail: R4.2's fallback excludes 'a merge into another bead or spec branch'. AC-11(iii) has X merged into sibling bead Y ('Merge branch 'bead/X' into bead/Y') 'before landing' and expects 'both X and Y are identified'. If X does not also land on its own as 'Merge bead/X' on the spec branch, X has no admissible candidate in either scan, and the AC asks for the identification R4.2 forbids. State in the fixture that X and Y each land with their own merge, or state what identifies X.
